order: ORDER — the sub-items this change was asked to deliver: 1. Stop answering "is this scratch directory inside the repository?" by comparing path strings. Windows reports `C:\Users\RUNNER~1\...` (an 8.3 short name) where realpath gives `C:\Users\runneradmin\...`; macOS reports `/private/var/...` where the caller holds `/var/...`; separators and case differ on both. Each of those made a directory plainly inside the repository compare as outside, which silently voids the guarantee that a review must not write into the tree it is reviewing. Ask git instead: run `rev-parse --show-toplevel` from BOTH the project and the candidate scratch location and compare git's two answers, which are in the same form by construction. The same work tree means inside it, whatever the strings look like; a different repository is genuinely outside, which is a legitimate place to keep scratch. Keep string comparison only as the backstop for a candidate git cannot see, and make that backstop tolerate separators and case where the filesystem does. 2. Route EVERY place that asks that question through the new git-backed check — both the pre-creation validation of a configured scratch root (the one that must refuse before anything is created, because "a review must not write into the tree it is reviewing" is broken by the `mkdir` itself, not only by the worktree that lands in it) and the post-creation check on the scratch directory the runner picks for itself. A candidate that does not exist yet must still be answered, by running git from the deepest ancestor of it that does exist. 3. Make the orphan-scratch sweep report the work it actually did. It counted only successful directory removals, so it reported "reclaimed 0" after reconciling git's records: on Windows the killed runner's engine child outlives it and holds the directory open, so the removal fails while the deregistration succeeds — the normal case there, not the exception. Count a directory when it was deregistered OR removed, and name any directory that could not be deleted as the harmless leftover it is. 4. The git-isolation negative control — with isolation off, git should complain about an unreadable global config path — does not reproduce under Git for Windows, which resolves HOME/XDG differently. Rather than fail the runner for its platform's diagnostics, or let a silent pass imply a proof that did not happen, have that control report itself INCONCLUSIVE by name where it does not reproduce, while it still reproduces on Linux and macOS.
claims: "Is this scratch directory inside the repository?" is no longer answered from path strings. `rev-parse --show-toplevel` now runs from the project and from the candidate — from the deepest ancestor of the candidate that exists, when the candidate itself has not been created yet — and git's two answers are compared, which are in the same form by construction. A different work tree is reported as genuinely outside, which is a legitimate place to keep scratch. String comparison survives only as the backstop for a candidate git cannot see, and that backstop now normalises separators and case where the filesystem is insensitive. All 2 call sites that ask that question were converted: the pre-creation validation of a configured scratch root and the post-creation check on the runner's own scratch directory. Verified by grepping the runner after the change — the string-comparison helper is referenced exactly once, from inside the new git-backed check as its fallback, and from nowhere else — and confirmed by hand on a short-name path (`C:\Users\RUNNER~1\...` against a repository realpathed to `C:\Users\runneradmin\...`): both gates now refuse, where before the change the pre-creation gate let that path through and the directory was created inside the tree under review. The orphan sweep counts a directory when it deregistered the worktree OR removed the directory, and names any directory it could not delete as the harmless leftover it is. Exercised by killing a runner mid-review on Windows, where the engine child holds the directory open: the sweep reported one reclaimed worktree and named the leftover, where it previously reported "reclaimed 0". The git-isolation negative control reports itself INCONCLUSIVE by name where it does not reproduce, and still reproduces on Linux and macOS, so the positive assertions there are not passing vacuously.
